fixes.explanation: Close to the neighborhood, friend, but not quite the address. Peter says their hope goes on "…the grace to be given you…" and grace is a gift, so nobody earns it with a punch card. It's given at the revelation of Jesus Christ. I've stamped a lot of cookies and not one of them paid for a gift like that.

That's True, baker. Peter says, "…it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed…" Silver and gold are the things you'd expect to pay with. Peter says that's not what bought them back, and he tells us what did in the next verse.

That's the answer. Peter says they were redeemed "…with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot." Precious is Peter's word for it, and it fits. Not silver, not gold, but the blood of Christ.

That's not what Peter points to, friend. He says they were redeemed "…with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot." Prayers of the prophets don't come up in this verse. It's one answer, and it's Christ. Peter keeps the spotlight right on Him.

Good guess if you're thinking of big moments in Israel's story, but Peter says something different. Christ "…was revealed in the last times for your sake." Moses isn't in this verse. The timing is the last times, and the sake is theirs.

Right, baker. Peter says they've been born again "…through the living and enduring word of God." Living and enduring, both at once. Peter even sets it against "perishable seed," and says this seed is imperishable (1 Peter 1:23).

I get why you'd pick it, but that's not what Peter names. He says the new birth came "…through the living and enduring word of God." The word is what does it. Peter doesn't point to the people who brought the message here. He points to the word.
